title: Supreme Court Directs RBI to Frame a Uniform SOP for Banks Handling Mule Accounts Linked to Cyber Fraud
case_name: In Re: Victims of Digital Arrest Related to Forged Documents
citation: Suo Motu Writ Petition (Criminal) No. 3 of 2025, order dated 4 August 2026
card_summary: In a suo motu proceeding on digital arrest scams, the Supreme Court directed RBI to prepare, within four weeks, a standard operating procedure for banks handling mule accounts and accounts linked to cyber fraud. The SOP must cover temporary debit holds, grievance redressal timelines and restoration of defrauded money, with copies sent to every High Court's Registrar General.
card_tip: An account frozen as a suspected mule account in someone else's fraud case should be handled under the bank's SOP for redressal and restoration; ask the nodal officer which step applies if the freeze stays unexplained.
verification_notes: Selected for Banking & Finance because mule-account freezes affect a large and growing number of ordinary bank customers caught up in fraud chains they had no part in, a frequent complaint in Delhi NCR and Kolkata given the volume of digital arrest and cyber fraud cases reported in both regions, though no court-specific local angle exists since this is a Supreme Court suo motu order with nationwide application. Case title (In Re: Victims of Digital Arrest Related to Forged Documents), the suo motu writ petition number, the 4 August 2026 order date, and the four-week SOP direction to RBI are confirmed across three independent reports (Bar and Bench, Verdictum, Moneylife). Whether RBI has since issued the final SOP was not confirmed in this run and is not claimed; the card describes only the Court's direction, not the SOP's eventual content. Not previously covered on the site.
